newsitem.title: USA: Mont. Colstrip 700 MW coal-fired unit at capacity.
newsitem.headline: Mont. Colstrip 700 MW coal-fired unit at capacity.

text.p: As expected, the 700 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant near Billings, Mont., returned to full capacity Thursday afternoon, sources familiar with the plant's operations said.
The unit was shut Tuesday morning due to a tube leak.
Colstrip's other units, two at 330 MW and another at 700 MW, were said to be operating normally.
Montana Power is the operator of Colstrip unit 4 and is responsible for the sale of 30 percent of its power output under long-term contracts.

Equity owners include Puget Sound Power and Light Co, Washington Water Power Co, Portland General Electric Co, Pacific Power and Light, and a consortium of GE Credit, Shell Oil Co and a lease-back firm.
